label: #3593502: scalable Menu tree UI with review fixes, pinned core
description: Compare unchanged Drupal core with MR !15975 plus the lab interdiff. The patched side adds the experimental Menu tree UI and the review fixes for CSRF readiness, search-result dismissal coverage, and forced-colours move affordances.
status: DRAFT: patch stack validated statically; DDEV, PHPUnit, browser, performance, and manual accessibility testing pending

steps.text: The recipe creates the same 15,000-link Main navigation menu on both sites. It enables Menu tree UI only where the MR has added it.
On /admin/structure/menu, open the Main navigation row's primary action: Edit menu on Before and Edit links on After.
steps.lookFor: The changed operation label is intentional. Before opens the classic all-links form and may exhaust PHP's memory limit. After opens the experimental tree UI and initially renders only the top level.

steps.text: In After, use the search field, press Escape, then repeat the search and click the page heading.
steps.lookFor: The results close in both cases while the query remains in the search field.

steps.text: Reload After and immediately toggle the first Enabled checkbox, then reload again after the request finishes.
steps.lookFor: The checkbox waits for the CSRF token if necessary, sends no empty token, and the new value persists.

steps.text: Use Space and the arrow keys to pick up and move a row, then cancel with Escape. Repeat with the pointer.
steps.lookFor: Reordering is unavailable until initialization finishes. Afterwards, pickup, destination, cancellation, focus, and announcements remain coherent.

steps.text: Open the forced-colours window and repeat the move interaction in forced light and forced dark.
steps.lookFor: The move handle, grabbed or target outline, focus indicator, and drop position remain visible.

steps.text: For a direct classic-form comparison, open /admin/structure/menu/manage/main on Before and /admin/structure/menu/manage/main/links on After.
steps.lookFor: Both classic routes may exhaust the configured memory limit. The MR retains that form as a no-JavaScript fallback; the scalable replacement is the After side's /tree route.

expected: After provides the experimental scalable menu tree and the interdiff prevents early CSRF failures, covers both search dismissal paths, and keeps move affordances visible in forced colours.
actual: Before has only the classic all-links form. After is MR !15975 plus the proposed interdiff. Runtime verification is pending.

checks.label: The menu search control is present
The initial tree is bounded to at most 200 rendered rows
Reordering reports ready after the CSRF token resolves

observe.label: The scalable Menu tree UI loads and remains responsive
Escape and an outside click dismiss search results without clearing the query
An Enabled change made immediately after page load persists
Move affordances and destinations remain visible in forced colours
Every move can be completed and cancelled with the keyboard

manual: Keyboard navigation, reordering, cancellation, and visible focus
Search dismissal with Escape and an outside click
Move states in Windows High Contrast or the lab forced-colours window
Screen-reader names, states, levels, loading, moves, saves, and errors
Zoom to 200 and 400 percent and reflow at 320 CSS pixels
Touch and single-pointer alternatives to dragging
Performance and peak memory with 15,000 links
A wide level with 5,000 siblings and a parent with 5,000 children

label: #3593502: MR !15975 compared with the review interdiff
description: Compare MR !15975 as published with the same MR plus the lab review interdiff. Both sides use the same pinned Drupal core commit and the same 15,000-link menu.
status: DRAFT: intended for direct MR-to-interdiff review; runtime evidence pending

steps.text: The recipe creates the same 15,000-link Main navigation menu and enables Menu tree UI on both patch stacks.
Open the tree page in both frames and compare initial load, rendered row count, responsiveness, and PHP peak memory.
steps.lookFor: Both sides load the scalable tree. Neither should build all 15,000 links into the initial response.

steps.text: Reload both frames and immediately toggle the same Enabled checkbox before the CSRF token request finishes.
steps.lookFor: MR-only may send an empty token and reject or revert the update. After waits for the token, disables the checkbox while waiting, persists the change, and can restore it.

steps.text: Search for Lab seed 1.1. Dismiss the results with Escape, then repeat and dismiss them by clicking the page heading.
steps.lookFor: The interaction should work on both sides. The interdiff adds browser-level regression coverage rather than intentionally changing the visible result.

steps.text: Use keyboard and pointer reordering in forced-colours mode on both sides.
steps.lookFor: After keeps the move handle, grabbed or target outline, and drop indicator visible with system colours.

expected: Both stacks remain responsive with 15,000 links. The interdiff removes the early CSRF-token race and improves forced-colours move affordances without regressing search, expansion, or reordering.
actual: The two patch stacks are configured. DDEV, performance, browser, and manual accessibility evidence is pending.

observe.label: The tree UI loads and remains responsive with 15,000 links
An immediate Enabled change waits for a CSRF token and persists
Escape and outside click dismiss search results without clearing the query
Move affordances remain visible in forced colours
